# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QH (Cave 1), Col. 7 | **Condition:** Better preserved

---

**7:1** I thank You, O Lord, for You have set me as a source of streams in a dry land, a spring of water in a parched land.

**7:2** And a watering for a garden [...] a pool and a living spring.

**7:3** And You have placed a planting of cypress and elm together with cedar for Your glory.

**7:4** Trees of life at a secret spring, hidden among all the trees of water.

**7:5** They shall send out a shoot for an eternal planting, taking root before they blossom.

**7:6** And they shall stretch out their roots to the watercourse and its trunk shall be open to the living water.

**7:7** And it shall become an eternal fountain. And in the shoot of its foliage all the beasts of the forest shall feed.

**7:8** And its trunk shall be trodden by all who pass on the way, and its branches by all the birds of the air.

**7:9** And all the trees of water shall rise above it, for in their planting they grow tall.

**7:10** But they send not their root to the watercourse.

**7:11** And the shoot of the holy planting for the planting of truth is hidden, without being esteemed, and the mystery of its seal is not known.

**7:12** And You, O God, have fenced its fruit with the mystery of mighty warriors and spirits of holiness.

**7:13** And the turning flame of fire, so that no stranger may enter the fountain of life.

**7:14** Nor drink of the holy waters with the eternal trees.

**7:15** Nor yield his fruit with the planting of the clouds, for he sees without recognizing.

**7:16** And he considers without believing in the source of life. And he yields the bud of [...] the eternal fountain.

**7:17** And I have become the scorn of flooding rivers, for they cast up their mire upon me.

**7:18** But You, O my God, have placed in my mouth as the early rain for all [...] and a spring of living water.

**7:19** And it shall not fail, opening the heavens without ceasing. And they shall become a torrent overflowing.

**7:20** To the seas without end [...] and they shall burst forth suddenly, hidden from concealment, and they shall become [...] waters in abundance.

**7:21** For it was hidden from the eyes of all [...] and concealed from mortal man.

**7:22** And they were reckoned by Israel as of no account [...] and among the trees of water.

**7:23** But the planting of fruit [...] shall send forth its branch for an eternal planting.

**7:24** And it shall take root in all the earth, and by its branches all [...] trees of water.

**7:25** And they shall spread out their roots to the dry land and [...] shall flow forth.

**7:26** For it is a planting of truth that brings forth branches of holiness for an eternal planting.

**7:27** And all the rivers of Eden shall water its holy boughs.

**7:28** And it shall become a mighty tree with vast branches, and all the beasts of the field shall dwell in it.

**7:29** And its shade shall cover the whole world, and its crown shall reach to the clouds.

**7:30** And its roots shall go down to the abyss.

**7:31** They shall send out a shoot for an eternal planting, taking root before they blossom.

**7:32** And they shall stretch forth their roots to the watercourse.

**7:33** And the fountain shall be opened for a blessed planting, an eternal source.

**7:34** And all the beasts of the forest shall feed on its leafy boughs.

**7:35** And its trunk shall be trodden by all who pass over, and its branches shall sustain every bird.

**7:36** And all the trees of water shall not prevail against it, for the root of its planting reaches to the watercourse.

**7:37** And it brings forth its fruit in season and its leaves do not wither.

---

*EMET notes: Column 7 is the famous "planting" hymn. The central image — a tree planted by hidden waters that becomes cosmic in scope — draws on Isaiah 11:1, Ezekiel 31, and Psalm 1:3. The "secret spring" (7:4) suggests esoteric knowledge. The "turning flame of fire" (7:13) alludes to the cherubim guarding Eden (Genesis 3:24). "Trees of water" appear to be superficial competitors who lack deep roots.*
